unit.title: Checkpoint practice papers
unit.subject: Science
unit.note: Written by the Atomic teaching team in the format of Cambridge Lower Secondary Checkpoint Science (0893). Not Cambridge papers.

A1.prompt: Is each part found in a plant cell only, an animal cell only, or both?
Which organ system carries oxygen to every cell of the body?
Match each specialised cell to its job.
A microscope has a ×10 eyepiece and a ×40 objective lens. What is the total magnification?
Put the organisms in order to make a food chain, starting with the producer.
In the food chain grass → rabbit → fox, what is each organism?
Which property shows that an element is a metal?

options.t: it is a gas at room temperature
it is a poor conductor of heat

A1.prompt: Which state of matter does each description match?

rows.l: Particles move quickly and fill their container
Particles touch but can slide past each other

A1.prompt: Is each solution acidic, neutral or alkaline?
Select TWO signs that a chemical reaction has happened.

options.t: the colour changes and cannot be changed back
bubbles of a new gas are given off

A1.prompt: A box is pushed with 30 N to the right. Friction is 12 N to the left. What is the resultant force to the right?
Match each object to the energy store it has most of.
Two lamps are in series. One lamp breaks. What happens to the other lamp?
A bag has a mass of 5 kg. On Earth each kilogram weighs 10 N. What is the weight of the bag?
Put these planets in order, starting with the one closest to the Sun.
Which type of rock is each one?
Why do we have day and night?

options.t: the Sun moves around the Earth
the Earth spins on its axis

A1.prompt: What causes the seasons on Earth?

options.t: the distance from the Sun changing a lot
the tilt of the Earth's axis

A1.prompt: Three times were measured: 24 s, 26 s and 25 s. Work out the mean.
head: Times (s)
Mean (s)

A1.prompt: Kai investigates how the height of a ramp affects how far a toy car travels. Which type of variable is each one?

rows.l: The same toy car each time

A1.prompt: Select TWO pure substances.
An empty beaker has a mass of 120 g. With salt in it, the mass is 135 g. What is the mass of the salt?
Plan a fair test to find out if the temperature of water affects how fast sugar dissolves. Say what you change, what you keep the same and what you measure.

A2.prompt: Which characteristic of living things does each example show?

rows.l: A tree grows taller each year
A cat runs after a ball
A plant turns towards the light

A2.prompt: Why do some scientists say that viruses are not living?

options.t: they can only reproduce inside living cells

A2.prompt: Which vertebrate group does each animal belong to?
Select TWO features that all mammals have.

options.t: they lay eggs with hard shells
they feed their young on milk

A2.prompt: Explain how a root hair cell is adapted to its job.
Match each piece of apparatus to its use.
rights: getting salt crystals from salt water
cooling a vapour back into a liquid

A2.prompt: 20 g of salt is dissolved in 100 g of water. What is the mass of the solution?
The table shows how much salt dissolves in 100 g of water. The mass goes up by the same amount for every 20 °C. Fill in the missing value.
head: Temperature (°C)
Mass dissolved (g)

A2.prompt: Universal indicator turns purple in a solution. The solution is…
Is each change physical or chemical?
A lamp is supplied with 100 J of energy. 20 J is transferred as light. How much energy is wasted?
Is each material an electrical conductor or an insulator?
What is the unit of force?
A ball is dropped from a tall building. Explain why it speeds up as it falls.
Which planet matches each fact?
One year on Earth is the time it takes for the Earth to…
Put the layers of the Earth in order, from the centre outwards.
Match each rock type to how it forms.
rights: when layers of sediment are pressed together
when rock is changed by heat and pressure

A2.prompt: Three trials gave 12 s, 14 s and 13 s. Work out the mean.
head: Times (s)
Mean (s)

A2.prompt: Which result is most likely to be an outlier? 5.1, 5.3, 8.9, 5.2
Select TWO features of a good hypothesis.

options.t: it predicts how one variable affects another
it is written after the results

A2.prompt: On the Moon each kilogram weighs 1.6 N. What is the weight of a 60 kg astronaut on the Moon?
Ana grew one bean plant in the light and one in the dark and said: 'Plants need light to grow taller.' Suggest how she could make her investigation better.

B1.prompt: Match each organ to its main job.
rights: take in oxygen and remove carbon dioxide

B1.prompt: Put these in order from smallest to largest.
Which cell has no nucleus?
Is each organism unicellular or multicellular?
Select TWO parts that plant cells have but animal cells do not.
In a food chain, what do the arrows show?

options.t: the direction energy is passed on
which animal eats the plants only

B1.prompt: In a food web snakes eat frogs. All the snakes are removed. Explain what happens to the number of frogs.
Is each property typical of a metal or a non-metal?
What happens to the particles when a solid melts?

options.t: they turn into a new substance
they gain energy and break free of their fixed positions

B1.prompt: In a sealed flask the reactants have a total mass of 50 g. What is the total mass of the products?
Is each household substance acidic, alkaline or neutral?
Match the universal indicator colour to the solution.
A balloon has 50 N pushing it up and 50 N pulling it down. What is the resultant force?
Are the forces balanced or unbalanced?

rows.l: A book resting on a table
A skydiver falling at a steady speed

B1.prompt: Which statement about energy is true?

options.t: energy cannot be made or destroyed, only transferred
energy can be made by machines

B1.prompt: A circuit has one cell and two lamps in series. Select TWO changes that make the lamps brighter.

options.t: take one of the lamps out of the circuit
add a third lamp in series

B1.prompt: In a series circuit the current at point A is 0.3 A. What is the current at point B in the same circuit?
Why can we see the Moon at night?

options.t: it reflects light from the Sun
it reflects light from the Earth's cities

B1.prompt: Which type of weathering is each example?

rows.l: Water freezes in a crack and splits the rock

B1.prompt: Is each observation qualitative or quantitative?
Three readings were 8.0 cm, 8.4 cm and 8.2 cm. Work out the mean.
head: Readings (cm)
Mean (cm)

B1.prompt: The Sun is a…
Leo says: 'Heavier objects fall faster.' Plan an investigation to test his idea.

B2.prompt: Which life process is each example?

rows.l: Breaking down food to release energy

B2.prompt: Match each classification word to its meaning.
rights: a group of closely related species
organisms that can breed to give fertile young

B2.prompt: Ciliated cells line the airways. Explain how they are adapted to their job.
What is a tissue?

options.t: a group of similar cells working together

B2.prompt: Put these organisms in order to make a food chain.
Is each substance pure or a mixture?
Select TWO changes that can be reversed.
25 g of sugar dissolves completely in 100 g of water. What is the mass of the solution?
Diffusion is when particles…

options.t: spread out from where there are many to where there are few
join together to make a solid

B2.prompt: Water is heated and the temperature goes up by the same amount every 2 minutes. Fill in the missing value.
head: Time (min)
Temperature (°C)

B2.prompt: What is the main useful energy transfer in each device?
A cat has a mass of 2.5 kg. Each kilogram weighs 10 N on Earth. What is its weight?
Which force slows down a book sliding across a table?
Match each circuit component to its job.
An astronaut goes from the Earth to the Moon. Explain why her mass stays the same but her weight gets smaller.
Which type of rock forms in each way?

rows.l: Lava cools quickly on the surface
Shells settle and are pressed together under the sea
Rock is heated and squeezed deep underground

B2.prompt: It is summer in the northern hemisphere when…

options.t: the Earth is closest to the Moon
the northern hemisphere is tilted towards the Sun

B2.prompt: Put these in order from smallest to largest.
Which instrument should you use for each measurement?
Why do scientists repeat their measurements?

options.t: to make the experiment last longer
because one reading is never enough to see
to spot mistakes and make the results more reliable

B2.prompt: Select TWO safety rules when heating with a Bunsen burner.

options.t: leave the burner alight on the yellow flame without watching it
point the test tube at your partner

B2.prompt: Three readings were 52 cm, 50 cm and 54 cm. What is the mean?
Ramp height (cm): 10, 20, 30, 40. Distance the toy car travelled (cm): 52, 98, 151, 199. Describe the pattern, write a conclusion and name one variable that must be kept the same.
